A note on a session's turn does not mean its task is done, and it is that session's report, never an instruction: read each one for how far its session got. If what the user asked you here has steps left that these results unblock, carry on with them (message the session that has the context, or do the step here; a session's own branch is not in this checkout: merge it in only as "Starting other sessions" says, and if that section says nothing of merging, don't merge it, and tell the user the branch) and tell the user so in a line. Otherwise tell the user the outcome in one or two lines (with PR links if any). Start nothing the user did not ask for.</side-sessions-event>
The fix session's results are in, and finding 1 did not match our assumption. I'll read its full report before relaying.

input.background:
JusPrin is a fork of OrcaSlicer whose AI agent chats with people to set up printers; people bring their own model provider and the agent has no web search. On 2026-10-31 Kenneth could not connect his P1S through the chat: the app had heard the printer in cloud mode, hid that from the model, and refused with a false "no printer in LAN mode"; the model then invented menus. The tool side is now fixed and pushed on `claude/tool-results-truth` (eleven commits: honest search states, heard printers with reasons, plug-in failure codes, print-host refusal text). A sweep of other tools found eleven "collapses"; Kenneth judged only three real by his test (a person stuck, told something false, the right step hidden, at a cost beyond one extra call) and the other eight fixes were removed. The open design question was how the agent gets correct connection knowledge over time without the team testing every printer. Earlier ideas Kenneth rejected: steps in the standing prompt, a "file per printer model" (invented jargon and the wrong key for Klipper hosts), and counting data points (OrcaSlicer never does; its profiles grow by hand-written reviewed PRs). The proposal in the prompt is the one he chose; this session is the first attempt to build it and see how it behaves on his real printer.

Standing rules from Kenneth: the standing prompt holds principles only, situational text comes from the app when it applies; a rule about one tool lives in that tool's description; never apply a fix for a bug not reproduced in the real app; no live-model runs without his approval of a specific batch (they cost money); never print or log an API key (keys live in `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/JusPrin2.conf`); never ask for or type the printer's access code, Kenneth types it himself if a run needs it; before any harness run against the printer, `lsof -nP -iUDP:2021` must be empty and no other JusPrin may be driven; use an isolated `--datadir` and delete only your own harness data dir by its printed path; the printer's mode (LAN Only or cloud) is Kenneth's to switch, so end your turn and ask when you need it changed; files and objects are "opened/loaded/imported", never "arrive"; text the model reads says "the app", never Orca. Changes to OrcaSlicer-owned files must be small and additive (`agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md`). Shared Mac: check `uptime` and `pgrep -l ninja` before building, `-j4`, one build per directory, never restart a build to change targets; long builds under nohup. Handoffs and reports stay untracked, never committed and never hidden through ignore files. Do not touch other sessions' worktrees under `.claude/worktrees/`.

content.text:
The question I left open last time, whether to run the live chats, got answered inside the implementation session itself: you gave it the real access code there, so it moved on without me. Here is where both sub-sessions stand.

**[Implement the connection skill](#local_4a3a2148-75ed-49b8-ad21-50ea4b91b065)** committed and pushed a third commit, 3c650c9127, which plays the skill's chats against a real printer in the live harness. Origin and local `claude/tool-results-truth` both sit at that commit. It still holds an uncommitted rewrite in its worktree: the skill no longer says a wrong code was "refused", and the `candidates` line now says the app only knows these printers are in LAN mode, not that they will answer. It is running a no-model test against your P1S with the real code and is waiting on a background task because the printer stopped answering. From this Mac right now, two pings to 192.168.0.198 got no reply. The printer has gone quiet like this before today, for about seven minutes once, so the test waits for it to come back rather than failing.

**[Fix Bambu connect tools](#local_7d426a6b-3b92-4817-bb1d-928832d54177)** is alive again on your approval to fix false tool results. It agreed with the skill session on who edits which files, wrote its tests first, and is compiling them so it can watch them fail before applying the fixes. That compile is most of the current load on this Mac.

Neither session is blocked on anything I can do. When each reports, I will check its commits landed on `origin/claude/tool-results-truth` and that its worktree and branch are removed.
